newsitem.title: UK: UK beet crop on course despite adverse conditions.
newsitem.headline: UK beet crop on course despite adverse conditions.

text.p: Britain's 1997/98 sugar beet crop is holding up well despite a combination of freezing overnight temperatures and a widespread lack of rain, beet experts said on Wednesday.

Although farmers took advantage of the mild weather in March to sow early and completed ground drillings ahead of last year, the head start could now be lost as adverse conditions take their toll, they said.
Weed growth has already been reported amongst the beets and one west Midlands crop has had to be re-drilled after mice destroyed beet seeds lying in dry beds.
Daytime temperatures have lessened since last week and farmers have been quick to apply low doses of herbicide to combat the weeds, which can stunt beet growth if left unattended.
But this could also cost farmers more money to grow their crop as more herbicide spray will be needed to eliminate the weeds.
Experts said farmers would have to use contact products on their beet as so-called "residuals" would have very little effect due to the dry soil.
The biggest problem appears to be the lack of moisture across growing areas.
"They (beets) do seem to be surviving...I don't think you can say there's any problem in the beet crop as yet," said an official at independent consultants ADAS.

"But I suspect if this weather continues for another week, we'll have a lot of red and blue leaves appearing as the crop gets very stressed and newly-emerged crops could perish as they search for moisture."
Beet scorch had not yet been reported, he said.
Patchy emergence will be another problem as the bed conditions have varied while drillings were taking place.
British Sugar said the crop was holding up well despite the dry conditions, as beet seeds were sown into beds which already had sufficient moisture content.
"At the moment parts of the country are dry - but where the seed has gone into good beds with moisture the crop is looking pretty good," a company spokesman said.
But the dry areas could naturally benefit from light rain, he said.
"In some of the areas people are irrigating to bring the crop on but they will rain to develop much further," the ADAS official said, adding that night frosts were not helping germination.
Independent forecaster WSC said variable clouds could be expected in northern Europe on Thursday with light showers from northern England into Scandanavia, far northern Germany, and northern Poland.

In its short-term outlook, WSC said there was an increasing chance of showers in Europe's northwest and scattered light showers elsewhere in the west. Temperatures would be near to mostly below normal.
